themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Ridgewood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 7 this week—a 1020% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.6 complaints per week—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or enforcement gap that emerged suddenly.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.74, severity: high)
Represents 1020% spike—most dramatic proportional increase in spike data
Timing suggests acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview DOE and Parks about any recent cleanup failures or contractor changes
Canvass affected blocks to identify whether tags are gang-related, political, or artistic; map geographic concentration
Check if commercial corridors (Myrtle Ave, Forest Ave) are disproportionately hit

themes_detail.label: Damaged street signs epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints hit 9 this week—a 260% spike from the 8-week baseline of 2.5 per week—with no clear external cause, raising questions about infrastructure maintenance or vandalism patterns.
evidence: 9 Street Sign - Damaged complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.5, severity: high)
260% increase suggests localized infrastructure stress or vandalism cluster
Aligns with concurrent graffiti spike—possible coordinated public space damage
reporting_angles: Request DOT asset inventory data on sign replacement schedules in CD 405 vs. citywide average
Check whether sign damage is concentrated in specific corridors (e.g., near transit hubs, retail zones)
Interview DOT about whether this reflects deferred maintenance or new vandalism pressure

themes_detail.label: Illegal posting blitz (two weeks)
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 16 two weeks ago—a 3100% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 per week (z-score: 15.5, the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset)—but has not been reported as ongoing this week, suggesting either rapid remediation or complaint drop-off.
evidence: 16 Illegal Posting complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 15.5, severity: high)
Highest z-score of all spikes—most extreme statistical anomaly in dataset
No follow-up spike reported THIS WEEK—unclear if issue resolved or complaints ceased
reporting_angles: Verify whether the 16 complaints were concentrated on a single block/entity (e.g., a specific landlord's buildings or a single event's flyers)
Check if DSNY or Buildings responded and whether enforcement action occurred
Determine whether complaint submitters are repeat reporters (e.g., neighborhood watch) or one-time incident spikes

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 6 two weeks ago—a 500% increase from the 8-week baseline of 1.0 per week—suggesting either new vendor activity or increased community complaints about street commerce on Myrtle, Forest, or Metropolitan Avenues.
evidence: 6 Vendor Enforcement complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.47, severity: high)
500% spike—significant but smaller than illegal posting or graffiti anomalies
No follow-up on this week's data—current status unknown
reporting_angles: Identify which neighborhoods are seeing vendor complaints (street vending hotspots: Fresh Pond Rd, Myrtle Ave, Cypress Ave corridors)
Interview street vendors and local business owners about licensing disputes, cart placements, or enforcement intensity
Check whether the complaint spike correlates with warmer weather or weekend activity increase

themes_detail.label: Root damage and sewer backups
themes_detail.summary: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints hit 16 last week—a 228% spike from the 8-week baseline of 4.9 per week—indicating accelerating infrastructure deterioration or tree-root damage that may signal systemic sewer or subsurface problems requiring investigation.
evidence: 16 Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.5, severity: high)
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for DEP sewer inspection and repair on specific street segments
reporting_angles: Request DEP asset data on sewer line age and repair history in CD 405; compare to citywide average age and condition
Interview residents on which blocks are experiencing sidewalk buckling, sewer backups, or root damage; map geographic concentration
Determine whether recent precipitation, seasonal tree growth, or deferred maintenance is driving the spike
Cross-reference with DOB permits filed for sidewalk cuts or private sewer work to identify problem corridors
